unit_name: Howard's line: the Continental light infantry and the Virginians (the main line)
notes: The third and main line. The staff ride calls it the Delaware-Maryland Regiment (+).
Picked men of the two Maryland regiments with the Delaware company (S98). Companies on the staff ride's chart: Beatty (MD), Kirkwood (DE), Anderson, Dobson (MD) (S95, p. 92).
Not placed on the map: no source read says where in the line it stood. It "wheeled to the right and attacked their left flank" (Seymour, S100).
The right of Howard's line. "Virginia regulars" to Howard (S98); Virginia militia on the staff ride's chart (S95, p. 92). Its attempt to change front began the retreat.

Two companies of Virginia riflemen, many of them former Continentals; Buchanan's Augusta men with Tate (S96; Neel, S101). Which flank they held is disputed: CH06. Ward (S92, p. 757) splits them: Tate on Howard's right, Triplett on his left; recorded under CH06.
Volunteers of North Carolina, South Carolina and Georgia. Pickens did not command them all, but they served in his line (S95, p. 93 n. 7). Maj. James Jackson of Georgia acted as brigade major.
Half of the skirmish line. On the right by Morgan's report, on the left by Hammond's notes: CH05. Ward calls him Joseph on p. 752 and 'Major Charles McDowell' on p. 757.
The other half of the skirmish line, with the dismounted part of McCall's state troops under Maj. Samuel Hammond (S99). On the left by Morgan's report: CH05.
With Lt. Col. William Farr. "A column marches up in front of Brandon's men" (McJunkin, S101).
Morgan writes "Hay".

unit_name: McCall's South Carolina state troops (dismounted part)
notes: The part of McCall's regiment not yet equipped as dragoons, under Maj. Samuel Hammond (S99); Morgan lists "McCall" on the left of the line (S96).
On the staff ride's chart and in McJunkin's list; no source read says where in the line it stood. Not placed.

Enrolled as dragoons the night before the battle and given sabres (McJunkin, S101; S103, pp. 64-65). Drawn as part of Washington's cavalry.
The whole British force. See CH04 for its strength.

unit_name: Light infantry (companies of the 16th, the 71st and the Prince of Wales's American Regiment)
notes: The right of the British line. One of its companies was provincial (the Prince of Wales's American Regiment).
The centre of the British line. Provincials raised in the middle colonies; many of them prisoners enlisted after Camden (S95, p. 56).
The left of the British line. Mostly recruits (S95, p. 76).
The reserve, then the left of the attack on Howard.

unit_name: Royal Artillery: 3-pounder with the right of the line
notes: One of two light 3-pounders ("grasshoppers"). The first part of the line advanced "under the fire of a 3-pounder" (S97). Ward's text (S92, p. 758) has the guns in the centre and on the left; his own map (p. 759) has them in the gaps either side of the Legion, as drawn.
"The other 3-pounder was given to the right division of the 7th" (S97).
The dragoons on the right flank (S95, p. 76), who rode down the militia and were met by Washington (Simmons, S101).

unit_name: British Legion cavalry: Ogilvie's advance guard
notes: Two troops sent ahead before dawn; then the fifty dragoons on the left flank (S95, p. 76).

Left on the ground of the night's camp till daybreak "under the protection of a detachment of each corps" (S97), about twelve miles from the field (S96); under Lt. Fraser of the 71st (S95, p. 85). Off the map; not placed.

unit_name: Eaton's brigade, North Carolina militia (first line)
notes: Men chiefly of Halifax and Warren counties (S138, p. 34). Which side of the road it held is disputed: GH04. Ward (S92, pp. 783-784) calls him 'Pinketham Eaton'; Davis (S150) and Hatch (S138) Thomas Eaton.

unit_name: Butler's brigade, North Carolina militia (first line)
notes: Chiefly Orange, Guilford and Granville men; Capt. Arthur Forbis's Guilford company stood in it (S138, pp. 34, 53). GH04.

unit_name: Singleton's two 6-pounders (first line, then the left of the third)
notes: In the road just in front of the first line; drawn back to the Continentals before the attack (Cornwallis, in S138, p. 43 n. 42).

unit_name: Washington's cavalry: detachments of the 1st and 3rd Continental Light Dragoons
notes: The right flank corps with Kirkwood and Lynch. Watkins's Virginia militia dragoons rode with it (S138, p. 77).

Three troops under Rudolph, Eggleston and Armstrong (S138, p. 24). The left flank corps with the Legion infantry and Campbell.

With Lee in the morning ("part of his riflemen", Greene) and on the left flank; the last Americans engaged (S138, p. 89).

unit_name: Lawson's brigade, Virginia militia (second line, north of the road)
notes: Regiments of Randolph, Holcombe and Skipwith, right to left (S144, p. 95). Which side of the road: GH11.

unit_name: Stevens's brigade, Virginia militia (second line, south of the road)
notes: Stuart, Moffett, Cocke and Perkins, left to right (S144, p. 98); a line of sentinels twenty yards behind it (S138, p. 37). Which side of the road: GH11.

unit_name: Huger's Virginia Continental brigade (third line, right)
notes: Two regiments of new levies under veteran officers (S138, p. 38).

Huger's own regiment, under Hawes for the day; the last engaged (S138, p. 83).

notes: The 1st and 2nd Maryland, with Jaquett's Delaware company in the line (S138, p. 130).

New levies; the left of the third line, by the road (S138, p. 38). Ward (S92, p. 784) calls it the 5th Maryland; Davis (S150) and the newer studies the 2nd.

notes: "In the curve of the line between his two brigades" (S138, p. 38).
